title: Dark Chocolate Cream Pie
summary: Deep chocolate custard set in a flaky blind-baked crust, crowned with lightly sweetened cream and curls of dark chocolate.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make and chill the dough
steps.text: Combine the flour, sugar and salt, then work in the butter until it looks like coarse crumbs with a few pea-sized lumps. Add the cold water a spoonful at a time, mixing with a fork until it just clumps. Shape into a flat disc, wrap it and chill 1 hour.

steps.title: Bake the case
steps.text: Roll out to about 3 mm, line the pie dish, trim and crimp, then chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan) and blind bake with paper and beans for 20 minutes. Remove the beans and bake 10-12 minutes more, until deep golden, so the base cannot turn soggy. Let it cool completely.

steps.title: Start the filling
steps.text: Whisk the sugar, cornflour, cocoa and salt in the saucepan, then whisk in the yolks to a thick paste. Pour in the milk gradually, whisking out any lumps; adding it slowly is what keeps the custard silky.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Cook over a medium heat, whisking and scraping the corners, until the custard bubbles thickly, then keep it bubbling for 1 minute more (it should pass 82 °C). Remove from the heat and stir in the chopped chocolate, butter and vanilla until glossy.

steps.title: Fill and chill
steps.text: Push the custard through the sieve straight into the cooled case and smooth it. Lay cling film right on the surface and chill for at least 4 hours, until firm enough to slice.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Whip the cream with the icing sugar until it holds soft peaks, swirl it over the pie and shave the chocolate over with the vegetable peeler. Keep cold until serving.

tips: Chop the chocolate finely before you start so it melts instantly into the hot custard.
The most common mistake is stopping as soon as the custard thickens; let it bubble for a full minute or it may turn thin overnight.
For neat shavings, warm the chocolate bar slightly in your hands and drag the peeler along its edge.
Wipe the knife with a hot cloth between cuts for clean slices.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Refrigerate, covered, for up to 2 days; add the cream topping on the day of serving if you can. Do not freeze.
